capabilities: Chat with multiple provider CLI agents in a tabbed side panel
Run inline edits on a selection as an accept/reject diff
Mention notes, folders, images, and MCP tools as turn context
Cycle Safe, Auto-approve, and Plan permission modes per provider
Show provider usage, quota windows, and spend next to the model picker
extras: Desktop only, no mobile build. Each provider needs its own CLI installed and authenticated outside the plugin; Grimoire adds no backend or telemetry. Provider capability support (rewind, fork, plan mode, image input) varies per provider and is documented in a comparison table. Debug logging is off by default and writes sanitized JSONL inside the vault.
intentEvidence: Grimoire brings agentic CLI assistants into Obsidian.
motivation: Built for people who already work in Obsidian and want AI help that behaves like part of the vault: local context, local files, a provider you pick on purpose, and usage you can actually see.
problem: Using AI coding assistants in Obsidian usually means a hosted plugin backend or copy-pasting vault context into a separate terminal, with no shared model picker, usage view, or permission control.

relations.evidence: Grimoire wraps the provider CLIs. It doesn't replace their account setup
runs on the Claude Code SDK, and supports slash commands, MCP settings, agents
Pick OpenCode for a model-agnostic agent that brings its own provider configuration

requires.name: provider CLIs (e.g. Codex CLI, Claude Code, Qwen Code, Pi)
provider account or API key for the chosen CLI
API key (alternative to OAuth/account sign-in for some providers)

summary: Runs local AI CLI agents (Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and others) in a side panel that reads notes, edits files, runs tools, and keeps session history.
